# Dfns


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A dfn is a function written in braces.
[`ω`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/omega.html) is its
right argument:

``` bpl
{ω×2}3
```

    6

[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) is its
left argument:

``` bpl
2{α+ω}3
```

    5

## Statements

A dfn returns the value of its last statement. Statements are separated
by [`◇`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/diamond.html) or
by line breaks:

``` bpl
{x←≥ω
 x×2}3
```

    8

The values of earlier statements are discarded:

``` bpl
{1 ◇ 2}0
```

    2

A statement can run for its side effect alone, such as adding each item
to a total:

``` bpl
{s←0
 {s+←ω}¨ω
 s}1 2 3
```

    6

A dfn that ends in an assignment returns the assigned value without
displaying it:

``` bpl
r←{x←≥ω}3
r
```

    4

## Scope

Names follow lexical scope. Modified assignment, such as `+←`, updates
the nearest binding of its name, looking outward through enclosing dfns
to the top level:

``` bpl
aa←3
bob←{aa+←ω ◇ aa}
bob 5
```

    8

Plain assignment always creates a name local to its dfn:

``` bpl
{gg←1 ◇ {gg←ω}¨ιω ◇ gg}5
```

    1

A dfn releases each local name after the last statement that reads it,
so the name no longer holds its array for the rest of the call. If that
array is the result of a [call that
waits](performance.qmd#calls-that-wait) and nothing else holds it, the
call then runs together with the calls that read its result, and the
result is never stored. A dfn whose text contains
[`⍎`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/hydrant.html) keeps
all its names, because the text that
[`⍎`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/hydrant.html)
evaluates can read any of them:

``` bpl
{a←ω ◇ b←a+1 ◇ b+⍎"a"}5
```

    11

[`⍎`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/hydrant.html) that
comes from outside the dfn’s text, as an operand or through a name bound
outside the dfn, can’t read a name after its last read. It raises
`VALUE ERROR`: “a has no value after its last read in the dfn”.

## Bodies and predicates

`;` separates a dfn’s bodies. A [predicate](glyphs/question.qmd) `C?`
tests the Boolean singleton `C`. When `C` is false, the dfn abandons the
body and tries the next one. This dfn negates a negative number:

``` bpl
{ω<0?-ω;ω}¯3
```

    3

After a predicate, a body can hold several statements:

``` bpl
{ω<0?a←-ω ◇ a×2;ω}¯3
```

    6

A name assigned in one body can be read in later bodies:

``` bpl
{a←ω ◇ a>9?"big";a>0?"small";"none"}5
```

    "small"

Every body but the last needs a predicate. If every predicate fails, the
call raises a `DOMAIN` error.

An empty body, such as `{}` or the first body of `{ω≡0?;ω}`, returns no
result.

## Arguments

In a call with one argument,
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) is
absent. An expression that uses an absent
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) is
evaluated as if
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) weren’t
there. Called with one argument, `{α-ω}` negates:

``` bpl
{α-ω}3
```

    ¯3

Called with two, the same dfn subtracts:

``` bpl
10{α-ω}3
```

    7

Anything computed only from an absent
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) drops out
with it:

``` bpl
{2×α - ω}3
```

    ¯3

In a list, an absent
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) leaves no
item:

``` bpl
{≢[α ω]}3
```

    1ₓ

Any other use of an absent
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html), such as
`x←α` or [`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html)
as an operand, raises a `VALUE` error.

`α←` gives
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) a
[default](glyphs/alpha.qmd), because the assignment runs only when
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) is
absent:

``` bpl
sub←{α←10 ◇ α-ω}
sub 3
2 sub 3
```

    7

    ¯1

[Valences](glyphs/circle-slash.qmd)
[`⊘`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/circle-slash.html)
joins a monadic function and a dyadic function into one.

## Recursion

[`∇`](glyphs/del.qmd) calls the current dfn. This dfn computes
factorial:

``` bpl
{ω=0?1;ω×∇≤ω}5
```

    120

A call to [`∇`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/del.html)
that is the last thing its body does reuses the current frame.

## Operators

A dfn that uses
[`⍶`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha-underbar.html),
its left operand, is a monadic operator. `twice` applies its operand two
times:

``` bpl
twice←{⍶ ⍶ ω}
-twice 3
```

    3

A dfn that uses
[`⍹`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/omega-underbar.html),
its right operand, is a dyadic operator. This one applies
[`⍶`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha-underbar.html)
between [`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html)
and `⍹ ω`:

``` bpl
2 +{α ⍶ ⍹ ω}- 3
```

    ¯1

[`⍢`](glyphs/del-diaeresis.qmd) refers to the current operator, for
recursion with new operands.

## Error guards

An [error guard](glyphs/error-guard.qmd) `kinds::handler` catches errors
of the named kinds in any statement or body after the guard. When it
catches an error, the dfn returns `handler`. `÷"a"` raises a `DOMAIN`
error:

``` bpl
{"DOMAIN"::0 ◇ ÷ω}"a"
```

    0

`∞::` catches every kind except INTERRUPT, TIMEOUT and UNSUPPORTED. In
the handler, `$e` is the caught error, as a record. `$e.message` says
what went wrong:

``` bpl
{∞::$e.message ◇ ÷ω}"a"
```

    "expected numeric elements"

[`•signal`](system/signal.qmd) raises an error of the kind on its right,
with a message on its left. The kind can be any one-word name that the
program chooses, and a guard catches it by that name:

``` bpl
{"NOTFOUND"::$e.message ◇ "no such user" •signal "NOTFOUND"}0
```

    "no such user"

## Design

BPL’s dfns come from Dyalog APL, with three rules from BQN’s
[blocks](https://mlochbaum.github.io/BQN/doc/block.html): the last
statement gives the result, predicates choose between bodies separated
by `;`, and an absent left argument drops out of the expression, as
BQN’s `𝕨` does.

In Dyalog APL, any statement other than an assignment returns at once,
so running a statement only for its side effect needs a workaround.

Marshall Lochbaum’s [five-year review of BQN’s
design](https://mlochbaum.github.io/BQN/commentary/fiveyears.html)
criticises two BQN features that BPL leaves out: choosing a body by
argument count and block headers. BPL uses Valences to choose a function
by argument count. The review finds that BQN’s rule for `𝕨`, which BPL
adopts, makes [ambivalent](terms.qmd#term-ambivalent) code easier to
write than tacit combinators do.

The review would also prefer not to determine what a block defines from
the special names in its body. BPL still does so. Braces whose body uses
[`⍶`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha-underbar.html)
or
[`⍹`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/omega-underbar.html)
define an operator. Other braces define a function.

Unlike a BQN block, a dfn keeps one scope across its bodies, as Dyalog
APL’s guards do.
